samples.question: At the top of the picture is a rack of four square slots in a row. Each slot holds one coloured disc, and the four discs drawn on the rack all have different colours. A single black triangle is drawn just under the rack: the queried slot is the rack slot whose centre is nearest to that triangle, and the triangle marks a place on the rack, never a particular disc. Below the rack is a row of cream request cards, applied one at a time in drawn left-to-right order, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries one coloured disc: that card asks for that colour. Apply each card by this rule. If the asked-for colour is already standing on the rack, nothing on the rack changes; the card only counts as a use of that colour. If the asked-for colour is not on the rack, it must be loaded onto the rack, and it takes over the slot of exactly one disc already there: the disc whose colour was least recently used, that is, the colour whose own most recent use is older than the most recent use of each of the other three colours then standing on the rack. The disc it takes over is gone from the rack, and the newly loaded colour now sits in that slot. A colour's most recent use is the last card, so far, that asked for it. A colour that no card has yet asked for counts as used before every card, in the drawn left-to-right order of the starting rack, so among such colours the one drawn in the leftmost slot is the least recently used. Loading a colour also counts as a use of it. Discs never move sideways: a slot only ever changes which colour it holds. Colours come from red, orange, blue, green and purple, and a colour that was taken over earlier may be asked for again later and then be loaded again. The rack is drawn only in its starting state: no later rack, and not the final rack, is drawn anywhere in the picture. After every card has acted in order, what colour is the disc in the queried slot? Answer with one word: red, orange, blue, green or purple.
